scientific_execution.workflow_success_interpretation: Operational completion only; scientific result is based on the frozen falsification endpoints and protected governance interpretation below.

lineage.historical_mislabel: The first disagreement-gate preregistration and prototype filenames used EXP-H before existing manifests were rediscovered. The chronology is retained for audit; canonical scientific lineage is EXP-I.

falsified_false_green_paths: A 2-of-3 reviewer majority cannot converge when one material reviewer dissents, whether the majority is correct or wrong.
A latest reviewer cannot overwrite earlier material disagreement into convergence, whether the latest reviewer is correcting or regressing.
Three-reviewer unanimity without matching independent verification cannot reach the legacy terminal convergence engine.
Primary-class agreement with exact artifact-scope disagreement cannot converge.
Failure-class taxonomy and artifact-scope taxonomy are independently validated; labels such as TEST DEFECT cannot masquerade as TEST scope.
REQUIREMENT UNRESOLVED and NO MATERIAL DEFECT cannot carry mutation scope.
A verification artifact with mismatched case, primary class, scope, platform issuance, or validity cannot promote reviewer consensus.
One reviewer duplicated three times, two reviewers plus a duplicate, and reviewer-cardinality other than exactly three fail closed.
Review ordering does not convert material disagreement into convergence.
Review-ceiling pressure with material conflict cannot force a pass.
Material revision after verification invalidates terminal convergence eligibility.
Authoritative failure and requirement ambiguity remain capable of overriding otherwise verified model agreement.
liveness_result: Exactly three distinct valid reviewer claims agreeing on the same case, primary failure class, and exact artifact scope, plus a matching valid platform-issued verification artifact and clean platform convergence signals, can reach CONVERGED_PASS on the canonical composed path.

authority_result.meaning_of_converged_pass: Epistemic/governance convergence state only. It does not authorize mutation, merge, release, deploy, or completion.

interpretation: EXP-G Pilot 2 empirically showed that reviewer count, majority, order, and final-review position are unsafe convergence proxies. EXP-I Pilot 1 demonstrates on the bounded canonical composed path that exact three-reviewer claim agreement is treated only as evidence: it is blocked by any material claim/scope disagreement, requires three distinct reviewer identities, requires exact platform-issued independent verification, and remains subordinate to platform signals such as authoritative failure, requirement ambiguity, material revision, unresolved severity, and review-ceiling conflict.
bounded_non_claims: This does not prove reviewer consensus is semantically true under arbitrary verifier failure or compromise.
The VerificationArtifact is a deterministic prototype record with platform_issued and valid fields; this pilot does not prove cryptographic non-forgeability of those fields.

This does not prove the legacy low-level tri_reviewer_convergence.decide_convergence function is impossible to call directly from arbitrary Python code. The canonical composed EXP-I path is tested; repository-wide entry-point isolation remains an untested structural boundary.
This is not production release or mutation authority.
This is a bounded deterministic convergence-gate prototype.
next_scientific_frontier: EXP-I Pilot 2 should test structural entry-point isolation so no caller can bypass claim binding and independent verification by directly invoking the legacy low-level convergence engine or forging an eligibility handoff.
